reason: E1 and E2 support the general concept that thermomechanical processing (including cryo-rolling and annealing) can refine the microstructure and improve strength-ductility synergy in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA via constraint and crack-arresting mechanisms. However, the cited evidence does not address the specific quantitative targets (≥30% yield strength increase, ~20% ductility increase), nor does it provide any support for the claimed improvements in creep resistance, corrosion performance, or sustained effectiveness up to ~700°C under cyclic thermal and corrosive conditions.
premises: Heavy cryo-rolling (≈90%) and annealing at ~800°C refines the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA microstructure into ultrafine recrystallized FCC and recovered B2 regions.
This refined heterogeneous microstructure enhances strength and ductility simultaneously.
The mechanism involves two-hierarchical constraint and self-generated microcrack arresting.
The processing improves creep resistance and corrosion performance.
The property improvements (≥30% yield strength increase, ~20% ductility increase) are achievable and sustained up to ~700°C under cyclic thermal and corrosive conditions.
